# Companion Product Requirement Registry

This is the canonical Companion product-decision and handoff registry. It is
not a second execution-status system: the current Codex Goal and this registry
are the current contract. Historical AIW plan links below remain audit context
only and do not replace the current Goal.

## Current Goal Precedence (2026-07-19)

The owner requested a new Goal after the prior Goal was no longer active. The
current Companion Goal is the Chinese physical-screen-recovery plus
component-Rig contract created on 2026-07-19. It first requires a healthy,
verified White/Black panel path before any real-panel dynamic-expression claim,
and retains the accepted deterministic V9/V22 browser/target behavior as a
protected inactive regression contract. The sole active inner-face source is
`companion-pet-expression-v9` with hash
`919F344957661DEF2099AD56AB1286CCA9DBA4D8F08B702617B6DF5B1A28E9DA`; the
sole pending menu source is `companion-menu-v7-screen-family` v7.3. The v6
root-only source is retained solely as rejected review evidence. Older visual clauses
that name v5/v6/v7/v8/v10+ art, a six-root home, or a camera as a daily art
development requirement are historical context only and cannot be used as a
visual source, fallback or current validation path. Daily visual work is
deterministic source-to-PBM/CEMP/render verification; a camera is final
physical preflight only when a healthy, aligned panel is available. The current
machine/owner/hardware boundary is recorded by the active Goal, this registry,
and its linked validation artifacts. The historical audit command
`tools/verify_companion_current_goal_audit.py` remains a required compatibility
anchor until its successor audit is explicitly recorded.

The current Goal-scoped actual-acceptance authority is
`docs/companion_goal_acceptance_contract.md` (G1 through G8). The earlier
`docs/companion_function_acceptance_coverage.md` remains historical coverage
evidence only; it must not override the current v9 visual-source gates, the
four-root menu, the lower-edge truncation recheck, or the CWF1 freeze.

On 2026-07-17 the two disposable Companion worktrees were removed after their
useful commits were classified; main is the sole attached worktree. Every later
resume must first read the installed `ai-collaboration-workflow` skill and
`<AI_WORKFLOW_REPO>\docs\agent_quickstart.md`; an unfinished active Goal must
not be falsely completed merely to rewrite it. The Goal API cannot edit or replace an unfinished active Goal; the same safeguard applies while that Goal is blocked. An owner-deleted Goal has no active contract and can then be
recreated under the current Chinese Goal rule.

## Current Visual Source Resolution (2026-07-17)

This resolution is the authoritative interpretation of all historical visual
rows below. A historical table row that still says `active` for a behavior,
acceptance failure, touch gesture, event contract, or portable API does **not**
reactivate any image, prompt, PBM, CEMP, menu layout, or visual validation path
named in that row.

- The sole approved inner-face input is `companion-pet-expression-v9` at
  `919F344957661DEF2099AD56AB1286CCA9DBA4D8F08B702617B6DF5B1A28E9DA`.
  Its CEMP is a 39-frame machine candidate only until the separate activation
  and physical gates close.
- `companion-menu-v7-screen-family` v7.3 is the sole pending menu visual
  candidate; `companion-menu-v6-four-root` is rejected audit evidence only.
  `system` and `journey` are the sole pending special-scene sources. None is a
  PBM/CEMP, Flash, firmware, or visual-PASS authorization before its recorded
  owner decision.
- Historical v5/v6/v7/v8/v10+ sheets, r1-r4/r4 menu art, six-root/two-page
  layouts, v15 style-lock paths, and all removed generated files are retired
  audit context only. They may not be restored, sampled, combined, prompted
  from, rendered, or cited as current visual evidence.
- `menu_v5_*` names are historical API identifiers only. They retain the
  portable four-root behavior, localization, navigation, and truthful-action
  contracts; they are not visual source identifiers and cannot select v5/r4
  artwork or a legacy CEMP.

## Read Order

1. Read the current Codex Goal before changing Companion behavior, hardware,
   visual assets, or acceptance scope.
2. Read this registry before changing the same scope.
3. Open the linked source document and validation artifact for the selected
   requirement. Do not infer completion from a `static` status.

## Steering Intake Rule

Every product-owner steer that makes a decision, rejects a direction, changes
priority, adds a constraint, or changes acceptance must be added or updated
here before implementation. A question without a decision stays in chat until
clarified. Replaced requirements remain as `superseded` with a replacement ID;
they are never deleted. Each active item must link to its authoritative product
artifact. Historical workflow-plan links remain audit context only.

## Current Handoff

The current implementation handoff is COMP-REQ-035 through COMP-REQ-039
together with COMP-REQ-006. The Denzic Platform recording-session core owns the shared
state decisions and Companion calls it through a target adapter. The latest
locked `4/13` run selected `通过` but correctly remained machine `NO_GO`: one
double tap entered `recording` and restored the SAI clock, then the same
implicit-boundary `DOWN` was re-armed as a phantom third contact. The recording
e-paper refresh delayed its release to `4303 ms`, dispatched menu long-press,
and ran before DMA start. There was no PCM, second double tap, stop, or external
Flash store. This run is not accepted.

The machine-first repair now passes. The captured coordinates and `4303 ms`
late release replay through the native portable C gesture core as exactly one
double tap and no phantom long-press. Recording provisional taps request no
display work, all other non-double-tap gestures are isolated while recording,
microphone DMA starts before recording status or expression requests, and DMA
is stopped on recording stop, cancel, and boot-probe completion so another
session cannot inherit a stale running flag and idle can return to low power. The
FT6336/static ordering, shared recording core, expression hook, strict log
parser, product registry, normal WB55 build and verbose-trace build all pass.
This is machine readiness, not physical acceptance. The next `4/13` run must
still prove clock, DMA, sustained changing PCM, no timeout, two double taps,
stop, and external-Flash store in one reset-bounded trace. The FTS02 analog
display fault remains recorded under COMP-REQ-034 and does not block serial
recording acceptance.

The first post-repair retry selected `失败` with note `无响应`; its reset-bounded
log had zero touch events. Audit showed that `build_verbose_trace` enabled trace
macros but omitted the normal SSD1681 bringup/menu/rotation/mirror defines, so
the flashed image was not a production-equivalent diagnostic. This failed run
is retained as tooling evidence. Before another popup, rebuild trace as the
normal product plus logging and require preflight ELF-symbol and image-hash
evidence; only the resulting trace can exercise the repaired behavior.

The corrected trace builds as the normal SSD1681/menu/rotation/mirror product
plus verbose logging. Preflight confirms the SSD1681 target,
recording-arbitration trace and DMA-stop trace in the ELF, rejects the stale
non-product trace, and rejects a 65-second capture window before hardware. This
enabled the production-equivalent retry below.

The next production-equivalent retry is also a retained product failure. The
owner confirmed both double taps and speech, then selected `失败` because there
was no visible response. Its trace recognized the first double tap, restored
the SAI clock, started microphone DMA and captured more than 50 changing PCM
blocks without timeout, but never recognized the stop double tap, stopped DMA,
or stored the recording. The evidence is preserved under
`.cache/validation/shared-recording-chain-acceptance-failures/failed-second-double-tap-no-visible-response-20260714-142920/`.

The follow-up machine repair gives FT6336 work priority before application and
microphone work, services it again after each bounded service, and suppresses
periodic e-paper expression work while a recording touch is being arbitrated.
The native host replay now proves two consecutive double-tap cycles; the static
scheduler gate, normal/trace WB55 builds and acceptance preflight pass. The
normal HEX is `94C9800928BB5022FE3282C755E28694F378AF9FBCF4A0DD4424C93DE0585B4E`
and the trace HEX is
`74F2EA593AF280A7EFC9DD8489CEC1D848DAEFBBA4B98DB23687E37E3B298448`.
No hardware was touched by these checks, so this remains machine readiness and
requires a new focused serial run. Visible recording feedback remains failed
and independently blocked by the COMP-REQ-034 FTS02 analog display fault.

That focused rerun on `b9424eb` failed despite the operator completing both
double taps and speech. It again recognized only the start double tap and then
captured 24 changing PCM blocks. The trace showed recording frames 53 through
57, repeated approximately 306 ms differential refreshes and a 1741 ms
maintenance refresh before touch sampling disappeared. COMP-REQ-038 therefore
replaces the pending rerun action with a stricter machine repair: touch-started
recording gets one initial status-frame service after DMA start and no periodic
application/e-paper work until stop or cancel. The normal image was restored
after the failed run; no further operator attempt is valid until this contract
passes host/static checks, both WB55 builds and preflight.

and reports cumulative PDM DMA overruns at stop. Static replay, parser tests,

not hardware acceptance: the next focused run must prove a maximum health gap
of 750 ms, two double taps, zero DMA overruns, stop, DMA stop and external-Flash
store; a remaining no-touch finding then moves to the FT6336/wiring branch.
